names.note: The calendar’s own name page for her is «Евфросиния (Джуринская), мц.»; the rank is stripped and the surname kept, the day line itself giving only «мц. Евфросинии». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

death.note: The year the day line closes with, «(1920)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 декабря ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Владимира пресвитера и мц. Евфросинии (1920).»

attestations.note: The second of the two the day’s sixth line names, and THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS: no life page stands behind her. «Мц.» is мученица, a woman martyr, and the name page repeats it and adds nothing else — no rank, no monastic grade, no place. `new-martyr` is written as this corpus writes it for this calendar’s twentieth-century entries. No folder held her: a Cyrillic grep for «Джуринск» over every `saint.json` returns nothing. The day page prints seven hymns and none is under either name.
